dct_description_sm:
Dryad version number: 5

Version status: submitted

Dryad curation status: Published

Sharing link: http://datadryad.org/dataset/doi:10.5061/dryad.k6djh9wj8

Storage size: 517140537

Visibility: public

Abstract

This dataset comprises a comprehensive collection of puma (Puma concolor) detections obtained from camera-trap surveys across Latin America, encompassing over 1,169,563 camera trap nights across 19 countries, spanning from northern Sonora, Mexico, to southern Patagonia, Chile. The compiled dataset includes 12,312 unique puma detections, together with associated sampling metadata and geographic coordinates.

Methods

Camera-trap detection data for pumas (Puma concolor) across Latin America were compiled from a network of over 200 contributors recruited through systematic literature review and snowball sampling. Potential contributors were identified via Web of Science, Google Scholar, and Scopus using keywords including "puma," "Puma concolor," and "camera trap," and contacted by email in September 2020.

Contributors submitted data in a standardized occupancy modeling format: each row represents a camera-trap station with latitude, longitude, and country, and each column represents a survey day, coded as 1 (puma detected), 0 (no detection), or NA (camera inactive). Data were also obtained from Panthera's internal repository (PantheraIDS). All data underwent coordinate validation and correction, date format standardization, and removal of records with missing or invalid locations. Two datasets unavailable for public sharing were excluded.

The final dataset is in long format, with one row per camera-station and date with confirmed sampling effort, and a binary puma detection variable (1/0). Files are provided in .csv, .Rdata, .shp and JSON formats.
dct_title_s: Data from: Collaborative camera-trap data set for evaluating the status of a rangewide carnivore in Latin America
